newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire Water sees capex surge in full-yr.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire Water sees capex surge in full-yr.

text.p: British regional water company Yorkshire Water, still struggling rebuild its infrastructure after being crippled by drought last year, said it would spend a total of 380 million stg on capital equipment during the current financial year, compared with 235 million stg last year.

Chairman Brandon Gough told Reuters in a telephone interview folowing the release of Yorkshire's first half results that capital spending to improve distribution systems as well as new water and sewage works had been about 180 million stg in the period. "There's about another 200 million to come in the second half. So that's almost a doubling of last year's figure."
Gough said that, within its first half spending, 170 million stg had been used to enhance its grid distribution system.

Capital spending would probably run at around 350 million stg per year for the next three financial years, he added, and within this, work would continue on a medium-term programme to improve customer confidence.
"At the heart of that is a further 130 million stg of capital investment" on other projects, Gough said.
